The chemical formula of table salt is **NaCl** (sodium chloride).

It consists of one sodium atom (Na) and one chlorine atom (Cl) bonded together in a 1:1 ratio, forming an ionic compound. When sodium (a reactive metal) gives up an electron to chlorine (a reactive gas), they form Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that are held together by electrostatic attraction, creating the crystalline structure we know as table salt.
